name: Chilli Parotta
steps: Knead 400 g flour with 230 ml water, 8 g salt and 20 ml oil until elastic. Divide into 8 balls, coat with 20 ml oil and rest covered for 1 hour.
Stretch each ball very thin on an oiled counter, brush with 20 ml more oil in total, pleat and coil into a layered round. Rest briefly, then flatten gently.
Cook the parottas on a medium-hot griddle using 20 ml oil in total until both sides are browned and the layers cooked. Clap to loosen the layers, then tear into bite-size pieces.
Heat remaining 45 ml oil in a wide wok. Stir-fry onion and bell pepper over high heat for 3 minutes so they retain some bite.
Add ginger-garlic paste, chillies and tomatoes; cook 4 minutes until tomatoes soften. Stir in tomato-chilli sauce, soy sauce, pepper and remaining salt.
Toss in torn parotta for 2 minutes until coated but still layered; scatter coriander and serve hot.
tips: Toss parotta into the sauce at the end so its flaky texture does not turn pasty.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
